title: Reason Code 265/286/287/295: the client certificate chains to a CA NPS does not trust
plain_english: EAP-TLS: the device presented a certificate, and NPS could not build a chain from it to a CA it trusts. The device and its certificate may be perfectly valid; the NPS server's certificate store is what decides. This shows up after a CA migration, when devices enroll from a new CA (Intune, SCEP, a cloud PKI) that the NPS server never learned about.

any: chains to an enterprise root certification authority that is not trusted
issued by a certification authority \(CA\) that is not trusted
does not chain to an enterprise root CA that NPS trusts

causes.cause: The issuing CA (root and intermediates) is missing from the NPS server's local machine certificate stores.
causes.next_check: On the NPS server open certlm.msc: the root must be in Trusted Root Certification Authorities and each intermediate in Intermediate Certification Authorities. Export the chain from a failing device's certificate to compare.

causes.cause: Devices enrolled from a different CA than the one NPS was set up for (new PKI, cloud CA, Intune SCEP profile).
causes.next_check: On a failing device, open the client certificate and read its issuer chain; then check that exact chain exists on NPS.

causes.cause: Code 265/287 specifically: the CA is trusted but is not an enterprise CA published in AD (NTAuth store).
causes.next_check: Run certutil -viewstore -enterprise NTAuth on the NPS server; publish the issuing CA with certutil -dspublish -f <ca.cer> NTAuthCA if it is missing.
